    http://www.example.com/query?cat=222&id=111

    and are equivalent (ie. they should return the same response).

    Another example are cookies used to store session ids. Suppose the
    following page is only accesible to authenticated users:

    http://www.example.com/members/offers.html

    the fingeprint. If you want to include specific headers use the

        fp.update(to_bytes(request.method))
        fp.update(to_bytes(canonicalize_url(request.url)))
        fp.update(request.body or b'')
        if include_headers:

                    fp.update(hdr)
                    for v in request.headers.getlist(hdr):
                        fp.update(v)

    return cache[include_headers]

    """Autenticate the given request (in place) using the HTTP basic access
    authentication mechanism (RFC 2617) and the given username and password
    """
    request.headers['Authorization'] = basic_auth_header(username, password)

    """Return the raw HTTP representation (as bytes) of the given request.
    This is provided only for reference since it's not the actual stream of
    bytes that will be send when performing the request (that's controlled
    by Twisted).

    path = urlunparse(('', '', parsed.path or '/', parsed.params, parsed.query, ''))
    s = to_bytes(request.method) + b" " + to_bytes(path) + b" HTTP/1.1\r\n"
    s += b"Host: " + to_bytes(parsed.hostname) + b"\r\n"

"""
Some helpers for dealing with scrapy.http.Request objects live here.
"""

from __future__ import print_function
import hashlib
import weakref
from six.moves.urllib.parse import urlunparse

from twisted.internet.defer import Deferred
from w3lib.http import basic_auth_header
from scrapy.utils.python import to_bytes, to_native_str

from scrapy.utils.url import canonicalize_url
from scrapy.utils.httpobj import urlparse_cached


_fp_cache = weakref.WeakKeyDictionary()


def request_fingerprint(request, include_headers=None):
    """
    Compute the fingerprint of a request.

    A request fingerprint is a hash that uniquely identifies the resource
    referenced by the request. As an example, consider these two urls:

    http://www.example.com/query?id=111&cat=222
    http://www.example.com/query?cat=222&id=111

    These are distinct URLs, yet both refer to the same resource and are
    equivalent (i.e. they should yield the same response).

    Cookies used for session ids are another example. Assume the following
    page can only be reached by authenticated users:

    http://www.example.com/members/offers.html

    Many sites keep the session id in a cookie, introducing a random element
    into the HTTP Request that must be disregarded when computing the
    fingerprint.

    Consequently, request headers are excluded by default from the
    fingerprint computation. To include particular headers, pass the
    include_headers argument, a list of Request headers to include.

    """
    if include_headers is not None and include_headers != []:
        include_headers = tuple(to_bytes(h.lower()) for h in sorted(include_headers))
    entry = _fp_cache.setdefault(request, {})
    if include_headers not in entry:
        digest = hashlib.sha1()
        digest.update(to_bytes(request.method))
        digest.update(to_bytes(canonicalize_url(request.url)))
        digest.update(request.body or b'')
        if include_headers:
            for hdr in include_headers:
                if request.headers.get(hdr) is not None:
                    digest.update(hdr)
                    values = request.headers.getlist(hdr)
                    for v in values:
                        digest.update(v)
        entry[include_headers] = digest.hexdigest()
    return entry[include_headers]


def request_authenticate(request, username, password):
    """Autenticate the given request (in place) using the HTTP basic access
    authentication mechanism (RFC 2617) and the given username and password
    """
    request.headers['Authorization'] = basic_auth_header(username, password)


def request_httprepr(request):
    """Return the raw HTTP representation (as bytes) of the given request.
    This is provided only for reference since it's not the actual stream of
    bytes that will be send when performing the request (that's controlled
    by Twisted).
    """
    parsed = urlparse_cached(request)
    path = urlunparse(('', '', parsed.path or '/', parsed.params, parsed.query, ''))
    lines = [to_bytes(request.method), b" ", to_bytes(path), b" HTTP/1.1\r\n"]
    lines.append(b"Host: ")
    lines.append(to_bytes(parsed.hostname))
    lines.append(b"\r\n")
    if request.headers:
        lines.append(request.headers.to_string())
        lines.append(b"\r\n")
    lines.append(b"\r\n")
    lines.append(request.body)
    return b"".join(lines)
